The poem

اقرأ القصيدة أولاً، ثم ادخل على كل مقطع: الكلمات، الشرح، والمصطلحات الأدبية. اضغط 🔊 لتسمع النص بصوت أمريكي.

Leisure

William Henry Davies

Stanza 1

What is this life if, full of care,

We have no time to stand and stare?

No time to stand beneath the boughs,

And stare as long as sheep and cows:

Stanza 2

No time to see, when woods we pass,

Where squirrels hide their nuts in grass:

No time to see, in broad daylight,

Streams full of stars, like skies at night:

Stanza 3

No time to turn at Beauty's glance,

And watch her feet, how they can dance:

No time to wait till her mouth can

Enrich that smile her eyes began?

A poor life this if, full of care,

We have no time to stand and stare.

The poet الشاعر

William Henry Davies 1871–1940

William Henry Davies was born into a poor family in Newport, England. His father died when he was two years old and his mother re-married and left her three children to be adopted by her parents, who owned a tavern. William behaved badly as a teenager and was often in trouble with the police.

وُلد ويليام هنري ديفيز في أسرة فقيرة في نيوبورت بإنجلترا. توفي والده وهو في الثانية من عمره، ثم تزوجت أمه مرة أخرى وتركت أطفالها الثلاثة ليتبنّاهم والداها، وكانا يملكان حانة. كان ويليام سيئ السلوك في مراهقته، وكثيرًا ما وقع في مشاكل مع الشرطة.

Paraphrase الشرح

The first stanza asks a question: what good is life if it is full of worries and if we don’t have enough time to simply stop and look at the interesting things around us? Life is not complete if we cannot stand under a tree, like a cow or sheep, and look for a long time at the beauty of nature.

المقطع الأول يسأل: ما فائدة الحياة إذا كانت مليئة بالهموم ولم يكن لدينا وقت كافٍ لنتوقف ونتأمل الأشياء الجميلة من حولنا؟ الحياة ليست كاملة إذا لم نقدر أن نقف تحت شجرة، مثل البقرة أو الخروف، وننظر طويلاً إلى جمال الطبيعة.

Literary terms المصطلحات الأدبية

Alliteration تكرار الحرف الساكن

  • Line 2: “We have no time to stand and stare?” — The consonant sound (s) is repeated at the beginning of stand and stare.
  • Line 3: “No time to stand beneath the boughs” — The consonant sound (b) is repeated at the beginning of beneath and boughs. The consonant sound (t) is repeated in time and to.

Assonance تكرار صوت العلة

  • Line 1: “What is this life if, full of care,” — The vowel sound (i) is repeated in is, this and if.

Paraphrase الشرح

Stanza two contains more examples of what we could stare at if we had enough time. What good is life if we cannot stop and see where squirrels hide their food in the grass and trees? Life will be dull if we cannot see the streams which, in the sunlight, sparkle and look like the night sky that is full of shining stars. The poet is giving these examples to get the reader to appreciate the beautiful nature that is all around.

المقطع الثاني يعطينا أمثلة أخرى يمكننا أن نتأملها لو كان لدينا وقت كافٍ. ما فائدة الحياة إذا لم نقدر أن نتوقف ونرى أين تخبئ السناجب طعامها في العشب والشجر؟ الحياة ستكون مملة إذا لم نرَ الجداول وهي تلمع في ضوء الشمس وتبدو مثل سماء الليل المليئة بالنجوم اللامعة. الشاعر يقدم هذه الأمثلة كي نُقدّر جمال الطبيعة من حولنا.

Literary terms المصطلحات الأدبية

Alliteration تكرار الحرف الساكن

  • Line 1: “No time to see, when woods we pass” — The consonant sound (w) is repeated at the beginning of when, woods and we.
  • Line 4: “Streams full of stars, like skies at night.” — The consonant sound (s) is repeated in streams, stars and skies.

Simile التشبيه

  • Line 4: “Streams full of stars, like skies at night.” — The sparkling streams are compared to the shining skies.

Antithesis الطباق / التضاد

  • Lines 3 and 4: “in broad daylight” and “at night” — daylight and night are opposites.

Repetition التكرار

  • Lines 1 and 3: the phrase “No time to see” is repeated twice.

Stanza 3Three

No time to turn at Beauty's glance,

And watch her feet, how they can dance:

No time to wait till her mouth can

Enrich that smile her eyes began?

A poor life this if, full of care,

We have no time to stand and stare.

Vocabulary المفردات

Stanza 3 · booklet

observe, answer.

Turn at Beauty's glance and look at nature.
يلتفت إلى / يلاحظ
Stanza 3 · booklet

make rich, make something more enjoyable.

A kind smile can enrich your day.
يُثري / يجعل الشيء أغنى أو أكثر متعة

Paraphrase الشرح

The poet wants to have time to look at the beautiful things on this Earth. The beautiful nature of Earth has become like a dancer. The poet wishes he could have the time to watch her as she dances. Looking at the beauty of nature makes the poet smile and fills him with happiness. The poet thinks that our lives would be sad, dull and full of sorrow and anxiety, unless we have enough time to enjoy the beauty of nature.

الشاعر يريد أن يكون لديه وقت ليتأمل الأشياء الجميلة على هذه الأرض. الطبيعة الجميلة صارت كراقصة. يتمنى أن يكون لديه وقت ليشاهدها وهي ترقص. التطلع إلى جمال الطبيعة يجعل الشاعر يبتسم ويملؤه سعادة. ويرى أن حياتنا ستكون حزينة ومملة ومليئة بالهم والقلق، إلا إذا كان لدينا وقت كافٍ لنستمتع بجمال الطبيعة.

Literary terms المصطلحات الأدبية

Personification التشخيص / التجسيد

  • Lines 2–4: “And watch her feet, how they can dance: / No time to wait till her mouth can / Enrich that smile her eyes began?” — The poet personifies nature as a beautiful and graceful girl who dances and smiles.

Alliteration تكرار الحرف الساكن

  • Line 1: “No time to turn at Beauty's glance,” — The consonant sound (t) is repeated at the beginning of time and turn.
  • Line 3: “No time to wait till her mouth can” — The consonant sound (t) is repeated in time, to and till.
  • Line 6: “We have no time to stand and stare.” — The consonant sound (s) is repeated in stand and stare.

Assonance تكرار صوت العلة

  • Line 2: “And watch her feet, how they can dance:” — The vowel sound (a) is repeated in can and dance.
